summary: The refactoring removes the guard check for `user.address`, causing `getUserCity` to throw a `TypeError` when a user object without an address (or with a null/undefined address) is passed.

findings.title: Unsafe property access throws TypeError when user.address is missing
findings.description: Removing `if (!user.address)` causes `getUserCity` to throw an unhandled `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')` when `user.address` is undefined or null, breaking backward compatibility.
findings.verificationHypothesis: Calling `getUserCity` with a user object lacking an `address` property (e.g. `{}`) will throw a `TypeError` instead of returning `null`.

suggestedReproduction.preconditions: User object does not contain an `address` property.
suggestedReproduction.suspiciousBehavior: Function throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')`.
